Linear Regression with Multiply-Imputed SCF Data

Source: R/scf_ols.R
scf_ols.Rd

Fits an ordinary least squares (OLS) regression model across all five implicates of a multiply-imputed SCF svrepdesign object, and combines results using Rubin’s Rules.

scf_ols(design, formula)

Arguments

design

A multiply-imputed svrepdesign object from scf_load().

formula

A model formula (e.g., networth ~ income + factor(edcl)).

Value

A tidy data.frame with one row per model term, including:

  • term: variable name

  • estimate: pooled coefficient estimate

  • std.error: Rubin-standard error

  • t.value: t-statistic

  • p.value: two-sided p-value

  • stars: significance level (***, **, *, ., )

Additional metadata is stored as attributes:

  • r.squared: mean R-squared across implicates

  • AIC: mean AIC across implicates

  • models: list of raw lm() results (one per implicate)

Details

This function:

  • Runs lm() on each implicate

  • Pools coefficients and standard errors using mitools::MIcombine()

  • Computes model diagnostics (R-squared and AIC) by averaging across implicates

Use this function to generate inference-ready model output for multiply-imputed SCF data, with support for summary(), model comparison, or stargazer-style tables.

See also

scf_glm(), scf_update(), scf_MIcombine()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
scf_ols(scf2022, networth ~ income + factor(edcl))
} # }
